scope: Thiopurine dosing by TPMT and NUDT15 genotype, including azathioprine used for non-malignant immunologic disease.

keyRecommendations.text: Normal TPMT metabolizers start at full doses; intermediate metabolizers use 30–80% of the target dose; poor metabolizers need substantially reduced doses or an alternative agent.
Two loss-of-function TPMT alleles confer a very high risk of life-threatening myelosuppression at conventional doses.

NUDT15 poor metabolizers also need substantially reduced doses or an alternative, because loss-of-function alleles reduce degradation of active thiopurine nucleotides and predispose to myelosuppression.

clinicalBottomLine: Test TPMT and NUDT15 and reduce or avoid standard-dose azathioprine in poor metabolizers because of life-threatening marrow suppression.
notableCaveats: Most dose-finding studies were in a few diseases; CPIC extrapolates the pharmacokinetic recommendations more broadly. Mercaptopurine milligram examples are not copied onto azathioprine as if they were the same milligram schedule.
